newsitem.title: SWEDEN: FORECAST-S-E-Banken Q1 profit seen 1.38 bln Skr.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-S-E-Banken Q1 profit seen 1.38 bln Skr.

text.p: Swedish bank S-E-Banken is expected to average a first quarter operating profit after credit losses of 1.38 billion crowns, up from 1.35 billion, a Reuter poll of 11 analysts showed on Friday.
The forecasts range from 1.09 billion crowns and 1.55 billion. Loan losses are expected to decrease to 325 million crowns on average from 433 million crowns in the corresponding year earlier quarter.
Analysts will scrutinize S-E-Banken's net financial transactions because they are not sure about how trading has developed and what effect bond yield fluctuations have had.

For the full-year 1997, operating profit after loan losses is seen falling to 5.36 billion crowns from 5.87 billion in 1996. Next year, analysts expect profit to slip further to 5.26 billion crowns on average.

Expectations for the full-year 1997 have been raised 2.2 percent on average since Reuters' poll ahead of the 1996 annual report when analysts targeted a profit of 5.24 billion crowns. The report will be released on Tuesday April 29.
Analysts interviewed came from Aros, Carnegie, Den Norske Bank, Enskilda, Fiba Nordic, Goldman Sachs, Handelsbanken, J.P. Morgan, James Capel, Lehman Brothers and Swedbank.
